section_summary: This section comprises United States Embassy Tokyo monthly political reports for May, June, and July 1932, alongside accompanying Department of State Far Eastern Affairs division memoranda and enclosed Diet addresses. It documents the grave domestic political crisis sparked by the May 15 assassination of Prime Minister Tsuyoshi Inukai, the subsequent formation of Admiral Viscount Makoto Saito's national coalition cabinet, and peerage elections to the House of Peers. International developments highlighted include diplomatic friction with the League of Nations and the Lytton Commission regarding the non-recognition and status of Manchukuo, the Shanghai armistice, and Soviet-Japanese relations. Domestically, the materials record acute agrarian depression, the passage of foreign exchange controls to curb capital flight, commercial disputes concerning the Gerli silk contract and Fushun coal deliveries, and the increasing political leverage of the Japanese military.

subfiles.about: Concluding section of Embassy Tokyo Despatch No. 634 reviewing Japanese political, diplomatic, and economic conditions during May 1932.
subfiles.summary: This concluding portion of the May 1932 monthly report discusses Japan's foreign relations, including the Geneva Disarmament Conference, tensions with the Soviet Union, and debates concerning withdrawal from the League of Nations over Manchuria. It provides an extensive account of the May 15 Incident, detailing the assassination of Prime Minister Inukai by young officers, Takahashi's interim ministry, and the emergence of Admiral Viscount Saito's national unity cabinet. Financial and industrial developments are examined, focusing on proposed legislation to restrict capital flight, the cancellation of the Gerli raw silk contract, and depressed commerce in Shanghai, ending with comprehensive lists of Embassy despatches and telegrams sent to Washington.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Despatch No. 634: Monthly Report on Conditions in Japan during May 1932 (Report No. 68)

subfiles.about: Department of State memorandum summarizing and highlighting key topics in Tokyo Despatch No. 38 enclosing the June 1932 monthly report.
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs (Laurence E. Salisbury)
subfiles.summary: Memo on Despatch No. 38 (June 1932 report): Soviet notes discounted by Japanese capitalists suggest border peace; Gerli silk contract cancelled; yen depreciating.
subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Memorandum on Tokyo Despatch No. 38

subfiles.about: Embassy Tokyo monthly despatch reporting on Japanese domestic politics, international affairs, and economic developments for June 1932, accompanied by legislative addresses.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 38 transmits Report No. 69 for June 1932, noting Ambassador Joseph C. Grew's arrival in Tokyo and Japanese rejection of President Hoover's disarmament proposals. It details external relations concerning Manchurian governance, the Dairen customs dispute, Franco-Japanese aerial navigation conventions, and internal politics surrounding the 62nd Diet session and rural relief demands. Financial topics include the enactment of exchange control legislation, the cancellation of the Gerli silk contract, and the fall of the yen, followed by routine schedules of despatches and telegrams and attached translations of Premier and Foreign Minister Admiral Viscount Saito's June 3 speeches to the House of Peers.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Despatch No. 38: Monthly Report on Conditions in Japan during the Month of June, 1932 (Report No. 69)

subfiles.about: Department of State memorandum summarizing important political, administrative, and economic points in Tokyo's monthly report for July 1932.
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs (Laurence E. Salisbury)
subfiles.summary: Summarizes the July 1932 report: reorganized Japanese authority in Manchuria, Sino-Soviet normalization talks, domestic economic distress, House of Peers elections, emergency finance laws and Fushun coal compromise.
subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Memorandum on Tokyo Monthly Report for July 1932

subfiles.about: Embassy Tokyo monthly despatch reviewing political, diplomatic, and economic developments in Japan and Manchuria during July 1932.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 81 transmits Report No. 70 on conditions in Japan during July 1932, covering the Tokyo visit of the League of Nations Commission of Inquiry (Lytton Commission) and Japanese resolve to recognize Manchukuo. It details Count Uchida's installation as Foreign Minister, military maneuvers in Jehol Province, the appointment of Count Hirotaro Hayashi to head the South Manchuria Railway, and the ongoing Dairen customs controversy. On the domestic front, the report surveys the Prefectural Governors' conference on agrarian destitution, Kenzo Adachi's political organizing, the merger creating the Shakai Taishuto, the seven-year House of Peers elections, and the industrial conflict between domestic colleries and Fushun coal shipments.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Despatch No. 81: Monthly Report on Conditions in Japan during the Month of July, 1932 (Report No. 70)
